reason: A sleep session made from what's actually on my mind before a deadline is a nice idea, so I'd try it at bedtime. But I already pay for a sleep app, and the free few-a-day covers the nights I'd remember to open it.
objection: Another subscription I'll forget to use. Half the month I just put on the same rain sounds and fall asleep.
would_change_my_mind: If after a couple of weeks it clearly beat my current app on the nights before big meetings, I'd swap one subscription for the other, not add one.

v1.why: A check-in form popping up at bedtime is the last thing I want.

v2.why: Tabs are easy and I can skip the questions and just go to sleep.

v3.why: Same as v2 but calmer; no scores staring at me at midnight.

reason: I'd sign up because it's free and I'm curious, but I've done this before: paid for Headspace, stopped after a month. I'm not paying until I see I'm still opening it in week three.
objection: I don't want an app asking me questions every day. My ring already tells me how I slept.
would_change_my_mind: If it read my Oura sleep score and built the night's session from it without asking me anything.

v1.why: Daily check-in sheet the moment I sign in, exactly what I don't want.

v2.why: Better, but the 'how do you feel now?' after every session would wear on me.

v3.why: The wearable hook is the only part that speaks to how I actually track myself.

reason: Free and made for me is worth a go on a night I'm scrolling anyway. Paying ten a month for something YouTube basically does for free isn't happening.
objection: I already have free apps and YouTube for this.
would_change_my_mind: If the free tier got cut so hard I couldn't use it nightly and I'd genuinely started sleeping better with it.

v1.why: Coins everywhere and someone else's chat; feels like a game, not sleep.

v2.why: Quick to type a line and hit play from the Create tab.

v3.why: Same as v2, the extras don't matter to me but don't get in the way.

reason: My commute is 80 minutes of headphones a day and that's the only time I get to myself; longer sessions built around how I'm actually feeling is what I'd use between therapy appointments. If it sticks through the first week, $10 is less than one coffee run a week.
objection: Another subscription I'll forget to use, like the last two I signed up for.

v1.why: The menu and percentages feel like a fitness tracker, not something I'd use alongside therapy.

v2.why: Chapters that change with how I felt fit a commute routine.

v3.why: Progress in words and a 'Why?' on each change feel closer to how my therapist talks.

reason: I'd tap 'Hard to sleep' once or twice on a bad night, but I paid for Calm and dropped it in a month; I'm not doing that again on my budget.
objection: I don't want to type how I feel when I already feel bad. At 1am I can barely type a text.
would_change_my_mind: If one tap on a chip gave me something genuinely good every time, with no typing and no follow-up questions.

v1.why: A form with notes asking how I feel is the exact thing I'd close.

v2.why: Least pushy of the three, but I'd still drift off it in a couple of weeks.

v3.why: Journals and reports are more things asking me to write about my feelings.

reason: I'd try it on the nights I'm scrolling instead of sleeping, and maybe mention it to my therapist. I won't pay until I can tell it's doing something a regular guided meditation doesn't.
objection: Will it actually help, or is it a gimmick? AI-written scripts could be pleasant noise and nothing more.
would_change_my_mind: A month where my own check-ins show I'm falling asleep faster, or my therapist saying the approach is sound.

v1.why: '60%, Great Progress!' on sample data is exactly the gimmick I'm worried about.

v2.why: Starts from my own words, which is the part that could matter.

v3.why: The 'Why?' and no fake percentages make it feel more honest.

reason: I'm not handing my mental health to an AI that writes scripts on the fly. On the commute I listen to podcasts by people I know are real.
objection: I don't want an app asking me questions every day, and I don't trust what an AI says back about how I feel.
would_change_my_mind: Scripts reviewed by a named clinician, and a clear statement of where my words go.

v1.why: An AI 'diagnosis' in the chat and a daily check-in, both no.

v2.why: Still AI building content about my mood.

v3.why: The 'Why?' is the right instinct, but it's still AI and I wouldn't use it.

reason: Before a stressful meeting I put on a five-minute YouTube breathing video and that does the job. I don't have time to make an account and describe my feelings to an app.
objection: I don't want an app asking me questions every day.
would_change_my_mind: If my partner or a coworker sent me a session they made that actually worked, and I could play it without signing up.

v1.why: Coins and check-ins, too much going on.

v2.why: Simplest of the three, but YouTube is simpler still.

v3.why: Journals, wearables, reports, more stuff I'll never set up.

reason: I'd try it to see whether my Apple Watch sleep data moves, but at $32k I'm not adding $10 a month for something I can't yet show is working.
objection: Will it actually help, or is it a gimmick? I want to see a number change, not be told I feel better.
would_change_my_mind: Seeing my watch's sleep data next to the sessions, with a real difference after a few weeks, and a cheaper tier around $4.

v1.why: The percentages look like data but nothing says where they come from.

v3.why: Linking my watch is the one feature that gives me real numbers, if it works.

reason: The private journal caught my eye, so I'd try it once or twice, but I've never paid for this kind of thing and the free one would be plenty.
objection: Will it actually help, or is it a gimmick? It sounds like a fancy YouTube video.
would_change_my_mind: If a friend my age told me it really helped her sleep and kept using it for months.

v1.why: Confusing menu and a coin counter; I'd be lost.

v2.why: Easier, but nothing there I can't get free.

v3.why: Nicest one, and the journal is nice, but I'd drop it the way I drop journaling.
